content: The primary risk factors for Clostridium difficile infection (CDI) are outlined as follows: 1. A reported prevalence of CDI is approximately 15% in the northeastern region of the United States. 2. According to Hensgens MP, Goorhuis A, Dekkers OM, and Kuijper EJ (2012), the risk of developing CDI significantly increases within a specific time interval following exposure to antibiotics. This study, published in the Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy (Volume 67, Issue 3, Pages 742–748), highlights the temporal relationship between antibiotic use and the onset of CDI. 3. Christina M. Surawicz (2013) discusses the clinical aspects of CDI in her article titled Clostridium difficile Infection, published in Medical Clinics of North America (Volume 97, Issue 4, Pages 523–536). This work provides a comprehensive overview of the infection, including its pathophysiology, diagnosis, and management. 4. Tim Planche (2013) provides further insights into CDI in his article Clostridium difficile, published in Medicine (Volume 41, Issue 11, Pages 654–657). This publication emphasizes the clinical presentation, diagnostic challenges, and treatment strategies for CDI.
